pageCache.pageTitle: Christ The King Catholic Primary School and Nursery - Home
pageCache.text:
To live together in harmony To grow & develop in Christ To reflect God's love in all we do
Thank you for visiting our website. Please contact the school office if you require any additional information!
Christ the King is a school where pupils are at the heart of everything.
Parents and visitors to our website will find key details about our school in the Key Information section, including admissions procedures, our curriculum, safeguarding and inclusion practices, and all statutory policies.
Our Catholic Life section shares more about the rich spiritual life of our school, our close partnership with our parish, St Mellitus, and the Religious Education curriculum that underpins our Catholic identity.
We are especially proud of our Outstanding Early Years provision (Ofsted 2025), and our Nursery and Reception pages showcase the exceptional start we provide for our youngest pupils.
You will find practical information for families—such as term dates, lunch menus, and clubs—within the Parents section.
To stay up to date with all that is happening at Christ the King, please visit our News and Events pages, where you can browse weekly newsletters, read our latest news updates, and view our live calendar of upcoming events.
Our Contact Us section provides details on how to reach us, along with helpful information about transport options.
We hope that your visit to our website gives you a clear sense of the warmth, ambition, and faith that define our school. Visits to Christ the King are warmly welcomed—whether you are considering joining our community or are already one of our valued families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ The King Catholic Primary School and Nursery - Our Catholic Ethos
pageCache.text:
Our Catholic Ethos
Our Catholic ethos is at the heart of our school, guiding our values, relationships, and daily life. It reflects our commitment to living out the teachings of Jesus Christ through faith, compassion, respect, and service to others. This ethos is important to us because it helps to shape not only the academic development of our pupils, but also their spiritual, moral, and social growth, ensuring that every member of our community feels a strong sense of purpose and belonging.
Our school is a place where Jesus is a constant presence in our daily lives, shaping all that we do. We are committed to providing high-quality teaching and learning experiences, with high expectations of both staff and pupils, ensuring that every child develops the skills needed to become an independent learner.
We promote equality of opportunity for all, ensuring full access to a broad and balanced curriculum, while celebrating both individual and collective achievements.
Within our supportive community, everyone is valued and respected, and we foster an environment where high standards of behaviour, self-discipline, and respect for the rights and views of others are part of everyday life.
We also strive to be a school where parents and staff feel supported in their roles, working together to nurture the whole child in a caring, inclusive, and faith-filled setting.

pageCache.text:
Our Catholic School
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
Christ the King Catholic School places Christ and His teachings at the heart of everything we do. Together with parents and parish, we seek to nurture the Catholic faith of our children and deepen their understanding of Catholic teaching and tradition. The vital partnership of home, school, and parish provides the foundation for lifelong religious formation.
We recognise parents as their child’s first educators in faith and work closely with families, offering regular opportunities for them to engage in the spiritual and educational life of the school through class assemblies, whole-school and class Masses, and clear communication about Religious Education learning and events.
In this spirit of openness and community, we warmly encourage potential families to visit Christ the King Catholic School. A visit allows you to see our provision in action, experience the loving, faith-filled environment we offer, and ask any questions about how we work together to support every child’s growth, learning, and faith journey.

pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching at CTK
Catholic Social Teaching is a set of principles rooted in the life and teachings of Jesus Christ that guide how we live together as a community and care for the world.
It emphasises the dignity of every person, the importance of caring for the poor and vulnerable, and our responsibility to work for justice and peace.
These teachings encourage us to build a society based on love, fairness, and respect, where everyone has a voice and the opportunity to thrive.
In our school, Catholic Social Teaching inspires us to act with compassion, serve others, and make positive contributions to our local and global community.
We use the Caritas resources and planning overview and look for opportunities to live out the principles in our faith throughout the school year.

Welcome from our Executive Headteacher
Welcome to Christ the King Catholic Primary School—a vibrant, busy, and friendly community with a proud history and strong Catholic tradition. I am delighted to extend a warm and heartfelt welcome on behalf of our entire school family, and I hope your visit to our website gives you a genuine sense of the faith‑filled, nurturing, and ambitious environment that makes our school such a special place for every child.
At Christ the King, the teachings of Jesus Christ and the values of the Gospel inspire all that we do; our Mission Statement and Five Keys are at the heart of daily life and guide us in ensuring every child is known, valued, and supported to achieve their very best spiritually, academically, and personally.
We set high expectations for learning and behaviour, believing that children flourish when both nurtured and challenged, and we work in close partnership with parents, carers, and our Parish to provide an education rooted in love, kindness, respect, and service.
Our website offers a snapshot of school life and up‑to‑date information for families and the wider community, and I encourage you to explore our weekly newsletter, which is emailed to all parents and available on the website. Please also follow us on Instagram to see what’s happening across our busy school.
Whatever brings you to our website, whether you are considering joining our community or are one of our existing families, please know that visits to the school are always warmly welcomed.

About our Nursery
The exceptional early years provision builds a strong foundation for learning, ensuring that children feel supported and inspired from the start.
Ofsted, January 2025
FREE FULL TIME PLACES IN OUR NURSERY FROM SEPTEMBER 2026!
CALL 020 7272 5987 FOR MORE INFORMATION!
Our nursery welcomes children from the term after they turn three years old until they begin Reception. We provide rich, meaningful learning experiences through purposeful play, ensuring every child has opportunities to explore, discover and grow.
We use children’s interests as a starting point for planning exciting, stimulating activities that spark curiosity, creativity and critical thinking. Children are encouraged to explore independently and collaboratively, developing essential skills such as communication, negotiation, investigation and problem‑solving.
Our highly skilled, active practitioners play a central role in supporting children’s learning. They observe play closely, model new language and ideas, and sensitively extend children’s thinking to deepen understanding and nurture development. Through intentional interactions, adults help every child to make progress while feeling confident, supported and valued.
Our aim is to enable children to become confident, independent learners who are well‑prepared for their educational journey. We provide a safe, engaging environment where every child is recognised as unique and encouraged to thrive. Our broad and balanced early years curriculum nurtures all areas of development—social, emotional, physical and cognitive—ensuring a strong foundation for lifelong learning.
We warmly welcome visits to our nursery. If you would like to find out more or arrange a tour, please contact the school office.
About our Nursery

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ The King Catholic Primary School and Nursery - Parents
pageCache.text:
Parents
At our school, we truly believe that children thrive when home and school work hand in hand. Partnership working sits at the heart of everything we do, and we know that the most successful outcomes are achieved when we build strong, positive relationships with our families. Your support, involvement and trust mean so much to us, and we value the role you play in your child’s learning and wellbeing.
We are committed to maintaining open, honest and supportive communication with all parents and carers. Whether through regular updates, meetings, workshops or informal conversations, we want every family to feel listened to, well‑informed and confident in the shared journey of helping each child grow, learn and flourish.
Our school community is enriched by the enthusiasm and presence of our families, and we warmly invite parents, carers and extended family members to join us at the many events we host throughout the year. These include our Christmas and Summer Fetes, school Masses, class assemblies, and a wide range of workshops and educational visits that offer opportunities to learn more about school life and celebrate children’s achievements.
We look forward to welcoming you into school often and working together to create a nurturing, joyful and successful experience for every child.

School clubs
At Christ the King, we are proud to offer a range of high‑quality wraparound and enrichment opportunities that support both our pupils and their families.
Our popular Breakfast Club runs daily from 8:00–8:40am, providing a nutritious start to the day for just £3.00 per child. We also offer fresh bagels for all children at the school gate each morning.
After school, our well‑loved King Club operates from 3:30–6:00pm, offering a safe, caring and familiar environment led by our own school staff, with engaging indoor and outdoor activities and a healthy snack included. King club is £9.00 per child per day.
Alongside these, we run an exciting programme of termly enrichment clubs—including choir, student council, sports and arts activities which give our children the chance to explore new interests and develop their talents.
Together, these provisions help ensure that every child at Christ the King has the opportunity to learn, play and thrive beyond the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christ The King Catholic Primary School and Nursery - Early Years Foundation Stage
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage
The exceptional early years provision builds a strong foundation for learning, ensuring that children feel supported and inspired from the start. This is an inclusive school, where everyone feels valued and welcomed.
The Early Years Foundation Stage applies to children from birth to the end of the reception year. At Christ the King Primary School children are admitted into nursery following their third birthday and into reception following their fourth birthday. Early childhood is the foundation on which children build the rest of their lives. At Christ the King Primary School we greatly value the importance that the early years foundation stage plays in laying secure foundations for future learning and development. However, we also believe that early childhood is valid in itself as part of life. It is important to view the early years foundation stage as preparation for life and not simply preparation for the next stage of education.
Children in our nursery and reception classrooms learn through play. They learn best from activities and experiences which interest, inspire and motivate them. We always use the children’s interests as a starting point, we provide children with stimulating, active play experiences in which they can explore and develop their learning. We provide opportunities through their play to think creatively and critically alongside other children as well as on their own. Play gives our children the opportunity to pursue their own interests and inspire those around them. The children learn to adapt, negotiate, communicate, discuss, investigate and ask lots of questions. We believe it is important that adults take an active and engaging role in child initiate play through observing, modelling, facilitating and extending their play.
During children’s time in the Early Years Foundation Stage at Christ The King:
The EYFS Curriculum
The EYFS is a very important stage in a child’s life as it helps prepare for school ‘readiness’ as well as preparing them for their future learning and successes. Children’s early years experience should be happy, active, exciting, fun and secure; and support their development, care and learning needs. Every child deserves the best possible start in life and the support that enables them to fulfil their potential. Children develop quickly in the early years and a child’s experiences before the age of five will have a major impact on their future life chances.
The EYFS Framework explains how and what children will be learning to support their healthy development and provide the foundation children need to make the most of their abilities and talents as they grow up.
The EYFS specifies requirements for learning and development and for safeguarding children and promoting their welfare.
Children will learn skills, acquire new knowledge and demonstrate their understanding through 7 areas of learning and development.
Children should mostly develop the 3 prime areas first. These are:
These prime areas are those most essential for a child’s healthy development and future learning.
As children grow, the prime areas will help them to develop skills in 4 specific areas. These are:
All 7 areas of learning are used to plan children’s learning and activities. The professionals teaching and supporting your child at Christ the King will make sure that the activities are suited to your child’s unique needs. This is a little bit like the curriculum in the rest of the school but it's suitable for very young children, and it's designed to be really flexible so that staff can follow your child's unique needs and interests.
Children in the EYFS learn by playing and exploring, being active, and through creative and critical thinking which takes place both indoors and outside. It is very important that they develop social skills, such as turn-taking, sharing and independence, which help them greatly in the next stages of their learning. The guiding principles that shape our practice in the Early Years are that children are born ready, able and eager to learn. They actively reach out to interact with other people, and in the world around them. Development is not an automatic process, however. It depends on each unique child having opportunities to interact in positive relationships and enabling environments.
This does not mean that all your child's learning is divided up into specific areas. One experience may provide a child with opportunities to develop a number of skills and concepts across several areas of learning. Your child's records will be passed on from either our Nursery and/or Pre-school groups, enabling us to ensure continuity throughout the Early Years Foundation stage. Phonics teaching and learning are a key part of the Foundation Stage and help to develop early reading and writing skills. If you visited Nursery or a Reception class, you would see a range of activities taking place such as role-play, practical games, painting, cutting and sticking and reading in the book corner. You would also see the outdoor classroom in operation, with equipment such as bikes, cars, sand and water.
Children work and play independently, with a strong emphasis on choice and being able to sustain concentration on projects, as well as joining a variety of adult-led activities. We encourage a partnership with parents so they are actively involved in their children's learning.
The EYFS curriculum consists of 17 aspects of learning. At Christ the King we provide our pupils with the opportunities the meet the Early Learning Goals in all of these aspects.
To find out more about the Early Learning Goals click the link below.
EYFS Statutory Framework
Communication and language;
Physical development; and
Personal, social and emotional development.
Literacy;
Mathematics;
Understanding the world; and
Expressive arts and design.
Assessment
Assessment plays an important part in helping parents, carers and practitioners to recognise children’s progress, understand their needs, and to plan activities and support. Ongoing assessment is an integral part of the learning and development process. It involves practitioners observing children to understand their level of achievement, interests and learning styles, and to then shape learning experiences for each child reflecting those observations. In their interactions with children, practitioners should respond to their own day-to-day observations about children’s progress, and observations that parents and carers share. To this end we make systematic observations and assessments of each child's achievements, interests and learning styles. We then use these observations and assessments to identify learning priorities and plan relevant and motivating learning experiences for each child.
At the end of Reception, each child’s level of development is assessed against the Early Learning Goals (above). Practitioners will indicate whether children are meeting expected levels of development:
Parents and Year 1 teachers will have access to the Profile report together with a short commentary on each child’s skills and abilities in relation to the three key characteristics of effective learning. These will inform transition meetings between Reception and Year 1 teachers about each child’s stage of development and learning needs and assist with the planning of activities at the start of Year 1.
